name: Mark Rutte
role: Prime Minister of the Netherlands (2010–2024), NATO Secretary General (since 2024)
summary: Liberal-conservative leader of the VVD who governed the Netherlands for almost 14 years. He combines market economics and strict budget rules with socially liberal positions on marriage, euthanasia and abortion, a tough line on immigration and integration, and firm Atlanticism.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme calls squatting a gross violation of others' property rights and wants it treated as a crime like burglary so that property is always protected.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The programme says the security services' powers must be adapted to new technology and communications so they can keep doing their work against terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He keeps hard drugs illegal and told the Senate he would advise everyone against soft drugs, while tolerating coffeeshops and testing a regulated supply chain.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme says family law rests on the traditional family although many families have same-sex or step-parents, and calls the traditional breadwinner model outdated.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The programme he led lists that gay people can marry as a normal Dutch value, and in the Senate he named gay marriage among the big issues that gave the Netherlands a lot.

abortion-legal.rationale: The programme says abortion must remain possible within the current legal framework, which he calls a good balance with the woman's freedom of choice.

free-trade.rationale: The programme supports a free market in Europe and trade treaties with partners worldwide as bringing jobs and prosperity.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme says the economy must be made to grow while fighting terrorism and aggression.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He told parliament the Netherlands disagrees with Germany on nuclear energy and called nuclear power, with gas, a transition fuel the cabinet wants in the energy system.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He said that one child inheriting from parents while another does not is part of a society with differences, which we should not be ashamed of, and that government's task is to help people in trouble.

one-party-rule.rationale: He backed support for civil society and pluralism in Belarus and more sanctions if repression continues.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He told the Tweede Kamer that it is the joint task of politicians to protect the fragile system of the monarchy and explain the reasons for the King's allowance.

direct-votes.rationale: The programme rejects any form of referendum at any level, calling it a simplification of questions and problems.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programme describes the society it stands for as one in which church and state are separate.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme says a government must not spend more than comes in and wants a structurally balanced budget with a spending ceiling.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The programme calls for a compulsory counter-contribution (tegenprestatie) from people on benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called the weekly table of ministers with trade unions and employers during the crisis, the polder model, an essential element of Dutch society.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In the government statement debate he said the cabinet wants to eradicate discrimination and racism altogether.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme says it is normal in the Netherlands that men and women, gay and straight, believers and non-believers are of equal worth with equal rights.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The programme says children in public schools should expect only neutral worldview education, not religious instruction replacing it.

population-transfer.rationale: The programme condemns the idea of expelling complete population groups from the country as fearful, not brave.

separated-powers.rationale: He told the Tweede Kamer the rule of law is firmly anchored in the Netherlands, with constitutional guarantees for the separation of powers, and elsewhere cited Montesquieu's separation of powers to explain why judges decide sovereignly.

party-controls-media.rationale: He called freedom of the press one of the priorities of Dutch human rights policy and backed funding free media against repression in Belarus.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The programme wants the naturalisation period extended to ten years.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme calls NATO the cornerstone of Dutch security policy and he later led the alliance.

minority-language-support.rationale: He told the Senate the cabinet considers the special position of the Frisian language important and is working on a law to support it, with extra funding for Frisian programming.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme states that the European Central Bank is independent.

collective-defense.rationale: The programme calls Article 5 the core of NATO cooperation, and as NATO head he calls the commitment that an attack on one is an attack on all a powerful message.

women-must-cover.rationale: The programme calls for a general ban on face-covering clothing in public.

common-currency.rationale: The programme defends the euro as a strong currency that works if everyone follows the rules, and would only expel states that refuse to reform.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The programme rejects statutory quotas for women, people of foreign origin or the disabled, saying talents and capacities, not sex, origin or disability, must count.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He said the best proof the Netherlands is a state under the rule of law is that his fiercest critic can say all this in parliament, which belongs in a democracy.

assisted-dying.rationale: The programme backs the euthanasia law and wants to widen the options, including for a completed life without a medical cause.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme wants a strong armed force able to fight terrorists and other enemies, and he later urged much higher defence spending.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme makes NATO the cornerstone of security policy, and after Russia's invasion he said the Netherlands is not neutral.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme wants to invest in more neighbourhood police, give the police full backing and lengthen maximum prison sentences, and says convicts must serve their full term.

rent-control.rationale: The programme says tenants and landlords in the free sector should be able to agree the rent themselves.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The programme wants a balanced budget with a ceiling on spending (Zalmnorm) and the Stability and Growth Pact strictly observed by all.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The programme says newcomers must see to it that they learn to speak, understand, read and write Dutch, and that making no effort has consequences.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme lists that women have equal rights as a basic Dutch norm newcomers must accept.

slavery-reparations.rationale: After the apology he said the government would not compensate grandchildren or great-grandchildren of enslaved people, offering a fund for initiatives instead.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: As prime minister he formally apologised on behalf of the Dutch government for the State's role in slavery.

notes: Searched the VVD 2017 programme and ParlaMint-NL speeches (marriage, abortion, euthanasia, drugs, nuclear, euro, referendum, Ukraine, rule of law, separation of powers, press freedom, racism, Frisian, monarchy, inheritance, polder model, markets, nationalism and patriotism, self-determination, minimum wage, unions, EU), plus NATO and government.nl speeches. Statements with no stated position (e.g. most nationalism, class-struggle and ethnic-nation items, and market claims where he spoke on both sides) stay null.
